title: Define the seam between the drawing kit and decade's renderer
body:
`draw.rs` in `decade/src/server/chrome/` holds `Scene`, a list of shapes in pixels with cell-grid helpers, beside `Paint`, which turns a scene into smithay GLES elements. `Shape` uses smithay's `Point` and `Size` as plain data. `text.rs` beside it holds `Font`, the swash rasterizer (`raster_run`, `raster_icon`) and `Text`. `Text` uploads each run as a `GlesTexture` and caches it under `(String, Face, color)`. `Text::new` reads the two font sizes from `Settings`. `Scene` imports `CellRect` from `decade/src/server/panes.rs`.

## Proposal

A new workspace crate, `decade-ui`, holds `Scene`, `Shape`, `Face`, `CellRect`, `Rgba` with the theme colours, `Font`, and rasterizing a run to a CPU bitmap. It defines its own point and size types and depends on no smithay. decade keeps `Paint` and the texture cache, which calls the kit's rasterizer on a miss. decade reads the font sizes from `Settings` and passes them to the kit as numbers.

`decade-ui`'s `Cargo.toml` names no smithay, so the compiler enforces the seam and no test scans the source.

## Decided

Jack signed off on 2026-11-19.

- Font sizes stay with decade's settings, and the kit takes them as numbers.
- The texture cache and its key stay with the upload in decade. `round_trip` and `pad` move with the rasterizer.
